segments.translation_text: "By this root of virtue, may the special noble intent of the holy lamas be fulfilled from height to height. May the precious doctrine of the Buddha, which is the source of happiness and benefit spread and flourish, the noble beings who are the pillars of the doctrine live long in good health, and the Sangha’s tenfold practices of Dharma increase from height to height. By the blessing of this, may the sponsors of this particular event, and the minds of all sentient beings swiftly accomplish the two accumulations, purify the two obscurations and their propensities, and swiftly attain the precious state of omniscient Buddhahood.

segments.translation_text: Or, "May all sentient beings abide in the four Brahma Viharas, i.e. abide in limitless loving kindness and compassion, joy, and equanimity. May they engage in the four doors of liberation: attain the samadhi of the door of the complete liberation of emptiness, likewise signlessness, wishlessness, and uncompoundedness. May they be able to benefit beings through the four social gatherings: through giving, likewise speaking gentle words, performing meaningful actions, and acting in accordance with Dharma. May they directly realize the suchness of the four noble truths: may they realize the entirety of suffering, be able to relinquish every source of its arising, actualize cessation, and meditate the truth of the path.

segments.source_text: ཅེས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའམ། ཡང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་ཁོམ་པའི་གནས་བརྒྱད་སྤང་པའི་དལ་བ་(ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག་ཅེས་སོགས་)དང༌། ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཆོས་བཅུ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་འབྱོར་བ་དང༌། རྟག་ཏུ་གཞན་ལ་ཕན་པར་སེམས་པའི་བསམ་པ་དང༌། ཅི་བྱས་གཞན་ ལ་ཕན་པར་འགྱུར་བའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། བདེན་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་གནས་ལུགས་རྟོགས་པའི་བལྟ་བ་དང༌། ཞི་གནས་དང་ལྷག་མཐོང་ཟུང་དུ་འབྲེལ་བའི་སྒོམ་པ་དང༌། ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་ཟིན་པའི་སྤྱོད་པ་དང༌། འཕྲལ་དང་ཡུན་དུ་ཕན་པར་འགྱུར་བའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག་ཅེས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའམ།

segments.translation_text: May all sentient beings possess the magnificent leisure of freedom from the eight unfavorable conditions, the endowment of the ten positive qualities, right motivation that thinks constantly of the welfare of others, right application that whatever is undertaken benefits others, right view that realizes the actual nature of the two truths, right meditation that is the integration of calm abiding and insight, right conduct that is associated with skillful means, and magnificent results that are of both temporary and ultimate benefit.

segments.translation_text: In the same way, may all sentient beings be able to: give gifts without expectation of reward and result; preserve immaculate morality without desire for rebirth; meditate the great wave of patience without resentment to anyone; perform great diligence which gathers every white deed; contemplate samadhi which completely abandons formless elements; and meditate special wisdom which is not separate from great compassion as skillful means.

segments.translation_text: Likewise, may all sentient beings excellently realize the inherent nature of the integration of the two truths, which is the Middle Way of the base; practice the application of the integration of the two accumulations, which is the Middle Way of the path; and swiftly attain the state of the integration of the two holy bodies, which is the Middle Way of the result. May they successfully engage in study in connection with genuine scriptures, contemplation which analyzes the unmistaken correct nature, and successful meditation in connection with the integration of method and wisdom.

segments.translation_html: Likewise, may all sentient beings attain unshakable faith in the three precious jewels, gradually enter the three precious vehicles, become skilled in the excellent meaning of the three precious baskets, rightly train in the three precious precepts, gradually turn the three precious wheels, and in the end attain the three stages of precious enlightenment.

segments.translation_html:
In every direction, may all those
Whose body and mind are sick and suffering
Through my merit, all attain
Oceans of happiness and joy.

segments.translation_text: May all of the infinite beings in the ten directions who experience the suffering of physical pain or mental unhappiness, through the power of my merit come to experience comfort in their bodies, and possess an ocean of limitless joy.

segments.translation_html:
As long as they dwell in samsara,
So long may their happiness never decline.
May these beings uninterruptedly attain the
Continual happiness of the Bodhisattvas.

segments.translation_text: As long as they abide in samsara, until they obtain the happiness of a Buddha, may all sentient beings never experience a diminishing of physical happiness and mental joy. May these infinite sentient beings engage in the conduct of the Bodhisattvas, and be able to attain the unceasing great happiness of unsurpassable benefit for other beings.

segments.translation_text: Reviving Hell: Those who fall into Reviving Hell find that due to their karma, a sharp weapon such as a sword appears in their hand. They regard everyone that they see as their enemy and hit and cut each other. Experiencing extreme suffering from these wounds, they faint and fall to the ground, at which point a voice is heard in the sky, saying "Revive again.” A breeze of cool air touches their body, and they revive to begin fighting as before. They continually experience this severe suffering until their negative karma is completely exhausted.

They cut along those lines using steel swords with blazing fire, or split the body asunder along those lines, using large and small axes. This is their type of suffering.

segments.translation_text: Crushing to Dust Hell: Those born in Crushed to Dust Hell are herded together into one place. Then the guards of hell cause the mountains on either side, which are shaped like the faces of goats, sheep, horses, elephants, lions, tigers, and others, to come crushing together so that all of the beings are smashed between the mountains. They bleed from every hole of their bodies. Again they are herded together and smashed in a huge metal machine, like sugar cane is mashed. Again they are herded together on the blazing, molten iron ground, and iron boulders tumble down from every direction so that the beings are smashed down like dust. This is their type of suffering.

When they enter it, the doors suddenly close and fire immediately comes from every direction. They scream and howl with a pitiful, mournful sound, and their suffering is that they can find no one to protect them from this suffering.

segments.translation_text: Hot Hell: In the hell named Hot Hell, beings' bodies are fried like fish in a blazing frying pan which is many yojanas in circumference. Blazing steel skewers penetrate them from bottom to crown, and flames burn from every hole and pore of their bodies. The beings fall down onto the molten ground where they are smashed by huge blazing hammers. This is their type of suffering.

segments.translation_text: Greatly Hot Hell: The Greatly Hot Hell is similar to Hot Hell, but the skewer has three prongs, like a trident. It penetrates the anus and the two buttocks; it goes up to the crown and exits from the right and left shoulders. The orifice of every organ completely blazes with fire. Then the body is wrapped and tied in a blazing iron blanket. Boiling iron liquid pours onto the head, and the flesh and blood are completely burned away so that only a few bones of the skeleton are left. These bones fall down to the burning ground and immediately reappear as flesh and blood again. This is their type of suffering.

segments.translation_text: Avici Hell: In Avici Hell, beings’ bodies lie upon the molten ground, with flames blazing in every direction. The skin, flesh, veins, and even bones and marrow are completely burned and the beings become nothing but a heap of flame that screams in great agony. One can only hear, but not see, that there is a sentient being in the fire. Some beings are fried like popcorn in a great frying pan with extremely hot, blazing sand. Others are forced to climb up and down a blazing steel mountain. Their tongues are pulled far out of their mouths and spread upon the ground, and pierced with many daggers. Their skins are peeled off and thrown upside down upon the blazing iron ground. Their mouths are forced open with metal and blazing lava is poured in, mixed with burning steel balls, which causes their mouths, throats, and internal organs to be completely burned to ashes. As the blazing iron exits from their lower passage, they experience tremendous agony. They must experience this terrible suffering continuously without ceasing.

As the blazing iron exits from their lower passage, they experience tremendous agony. They must experience this terrible suffering continuously without ceasing.

segments.translation_text: Next they come to an unfordable river that is made of hot ashes or boiling water, and their bodies fall in and sink. Both sides of the river are guarded by powerful guardians holding extremely sharp weapons. Thus the beings are cooked in the river until their flesh and blood are boiled away and their bones become as white as lily flowers. Sometimes their eyes are gouged out by iron hooks and they are hung upside down. The hell guards ask them what they want. The beings reply that they don’t know anything and can’t see anything, but they are hungry and thirsty. Then the guardians pour molten copper mixed with blazing steel balls into their mouths and the beings are completely burned. This is their type of suffering.

segments.translation_text: The Cold Hells: In the Blister Hell, an extremely cold wind blows on the body so that it becomes a mass of blisters. In Bursting Blister Hell, it is even colder and the blisters burst. In Chattering Teeth Hell, it is so cold that the teeth chatter with a loud noise. Brr Hell is even colder than that. In Alas Hell, beings are barely able to moan, "Alas.” In Cracked Like an Utpala Flower Hell, the skin becomes bluish, and splits in five or six different pieces, like the petals of an utpala flower. Cracked Like a Lotus Flower Hell is even colder than that, and the skin turns from blue to red and splits into ten or more pieces like a lotus. In Greatly Cracked Like a Lotus Hell, the skin becomes extremely red and splits into a hundreds or thousands of pieces. Thus they experience unbearable suffering.

segments.translation_text: The Semi-Hells: In the semi-hells, beings lack any certainty of place. Executioners are said to take birth as a large piece of food and their bodies are eaten by birds and other wild animals. Butchers’ assistants are said to take birth as a piece of bone that stinks with a strong odor and is eaten by crows and other birds. Fishers are said to be born with a body tightly bound by iron. Thus they experience great suffering.

segments.translation_text: May those beings who have fallen into cold hells such as the Blister Hell and other extremely cold places, find great happiness from warmth of sunlight and pleasant fires. Arising from the great clouds of compassion of the Bodhisattvas, may a great limitless ocean of water, and ceaseless gentle rain fall upon the hot hells such as the Reviving Hell, etc. May those weak from great heat in the hot hells find joy in being gently cooled by falling rain.

segments.translation_text: May the heaps of charcoal and hot ashes become heaps of precious jewels such as blue diamonds and red rubies. May the blazing hot molten iron ground become a cool and pleasant floor of crystal, clean, and beautifully patterned. May the iron mountains with faces of animals like goats and sheep, that crush and smash beings between them become a great celestial mansion filled with boundless offerings, and with the Bliss Gone Ones and their Noble Sons who work to benefit beings in hell.

segments.translation_html:
May those sunk in the unfordable river, like a fire hole, 
Flesh completely disintegrated, bones like lily flowers,
By the power of my virtues, attain the bodies of
Gods flowing gently with goddesses.

segments.translation_html:
Why are the hosts of the lord of death, crows, and vultures so terrified?
Wondering who has generated such noble power that dispels all darkness and creates happiness and joy,
Looking up, they behold seated in the middle of the sky, blazing Vajrapani.
By the force of great joy they are freed from their sins, and may they dwell with him.

segments.translation_text: May all the beings suffering throughout the hells suddenly see an amazing and auspicious emanation in the sky above them, and wonder why the guardians of hell, crows, insects, and fearsome vultures and others suddenly become petrified with fear and run in every direction. Suddenly, the dense clouds of dark smoke that arise from the burning flesh, blood, marrow, and fat of beings in the hells are completely dispelled by the light of compassion.

segments.translation_text: Whose great and noble power has brought this joy and happiness to body and mind? Looking up, in the center of the sky behold the great Bodhisattva Vajrapani, blazing with dignity and shining with light. At the sight, great joy and clear faith toward that Bodhisattva develop in the minds of beings suffering in hell, which frees them from their previous sinful deeds, and they accompany Vajrapani to ever enjoy great bliss.

segments.translation_html:
Seeing the fires of hell quickly extinguished
By a rainfall of gently scented water and flowers,
Thinking, "What has suddenly caused this satisfying joy? " 
May those in hell behold Padmapani.

segments.translation_text: As before, from the sky falls a shower of many different flowers mixed with fragrantly scented water and the unbearable fires and molten lava of hell are extinguished with a sizzling noise. Seeing it, the suffering beings are satisfied with happiness such as they never experienced before. Thinking, "Who could be the source of this great power?” they look upward and directly behold Lord Avalokiteshvara bearing a lotus in his hand. May those beings suffering in hell ever experience such great happiness together with this great Lord of Bodhisattvas.

segments.translation_html: As before, from the sky falls a shower of many different flowers mixed with fragrantly scented water and the unbearable fires and molten lava of hell are extinguished with a sizzling noise. Seeing it, the suffering beings are satisfied with happiness such as they never experienced before. Thinking, "Who could be the source of this great power?” they look upward and directly behold Lord Avalokiteshvara bearing a lotus in his hand. May those beings suffering in hell ever experience such great happiness together with this great Lord of Bodhisattvas.

segments.translation_html:
Friends, come quickly to us to be freed from fear,
Gaze upon the Youth with radiant crown ornaments who gives fearlessness,
Whose power frees from all suffering and gives rise to joyful strength,
Born from compassion and enlightenment thought to fully protect all beings.

segments.translation_html:
Lotus feet venerated by the crowns of hundreds of gods,
Eyes moist with compassion, a rain of myriad flowers falling upon his crown,
In an enticing celestial mansion, where thousands of goddesses sing melodies of praise.
Thus beholding Manjushri, may it still the cries of beings in hell.

segments.translation_text: They call to each other, "Behold Manjushri, whose beautiful eyes are filled with the moisture of great compassion toward every sentient being, upon whose crown falls a gentle shower of myriad flowers as divine offerings, and who dwells within a beautiful many-storied celestial mansion, which resounds with songs of his praise sung by thousands of daughters of the gods.” Directly seeing such an emanation of the great protector Manjushri, now the beings who suffer in hell cry out with a greatly joyful sound. May they experience great joy together with him.

segments.translation_text: The bodies of some animals are small, smaller even than one tenth of the tip of a hair, smaller even than motes of dust in a sunbeam. Some are as small as juniper berries; some are as large as ten thousand yojanas in length. Some elephants are said to be seven yojanas in size, and some sea monsters have a length of 2700 yojanas. Some nagas are as large as mountains. This is the general range of sizes.

segments.translation_text: Animals have various types of suffering. Some sea creatures such as fish and crocodiles swallow and eat many small fish. Many other small animals, such as maggots and insects, swarm together and eat the bodies of large animals from the outside in. Animals suffer from killing and eating each other. Some nagas suffer from a daily rainfall of hot sand until their flesh is dried to the bones. Some animals suffer from being eaten by vicious winged animals such as garudas and other birds.

segments.translation_text: The general meaning of the text is the wish that all animals may be free of their various individual sufferings and obtain great happiness. The specific meaning is, "May all of these limitless animals be free of the fear of harming and eating each other. May they have the temporary happiness of higher rebirth, and ultimately attain the unsurpassable happiness of ultimate liberation.”

segments.translation_text: The specific suffering of hungry ghosts is the weariness of suffering from hunger and thirst. Their physical bodies and their skin, flesh, and blood are as dry as a piece of wood that has been burned by fire. Their mouths are parched and their dry tongues are constantly licking their dry lips. Looking for something to drink, they are constantly searching for water in ponds and other places. Even if they see some water, they are kept away by weapon bearing guards who do not let them drink. If they find some unguarded water, it turns to blood and pus and becomes undrinkable. Hungry ghosts who suffer in this way are known as those with external obscurations.

segments.translation_text: If they find a tiny amount of food and drink, their mouth is as small as the eye of a needle, and their throat is as thin as a bowstring, so the food will not go through. Their bodies are as huge as an ocean and cannot be filled by food; their legs and limbs are tiny, and as thin as wheat straw, so they are unable to hold themselves up. Hungry ghosts who suffer in this way are known as those with internal obscurations.

segments.translation_text: The general meaning of the text is the wish, "May all hungry ghosts be free of the suffering of hunger and thirst.” The specific meaning is: For instance, beings dwelling on the northern continent known as Uttarakuru live where there is no private ownership, and they consume uncultivated harvests, things are produced by wish-fulfilling trees, and there is abundant material. May all the hungry ghosts in the infinite worlds of existence find food and drink in the same way, and successfully find every positive object that they desire.

segments.translation_text: Human beings also have countless difficulties and sufferings such as hunger and thirst, parting and arriving, being tired and weary, quarrelling and fighting, and being harmed and injured. Those who have possessions have the suffering of guarding them, and those who have no possessions have the suffering of searching for them. Others have defective sense organs. Added to this is the suffering of birth, old age, illness, and death. This dedication aspires to pacify all of these types of suffering.

segments.translation_text: May those who are terrified by kings, thieves, vampires, and natural disasters such as fire, water, and other fears, be completely freed from those fears, and may those fears never occur again. May those whose limbs, legs, and hands are bound by chains and fetters be untied and completely freed. May those who are weak and lacking in power and strength possess magnificent inner and outer power and strength. May they be free of conceit and pride, and always be friendly and gentle toward each other.

On boats and ships accomplish their intent;
And safely reaching harbor,
May they enjoy together with their relatives.

May they safely reach the ocean and river shore, return home safely and joyfully to gladly reunite with their friends and relatives.

segments.translation_html:
May those who wander sad and lost upon the path
Meet other travelers and
Swiftly reach their destination without exhaustion.
Freed from fear of thieves, tigers, and the like.

May they be freed of fear and harm by thieves, bandits and animals such as tigers, bears, snakes and other terrifying things. May they easily reach their destination without hardship.

segments.translation_text: This has six sections: 1. Dedication to obtain body and wealth, 2. Dedication to possess beauty and dignity, 3. Dedication to find magnificent virtue, 4. Dedication to obtain immaculate pure realms, 5. Dedication to accomplish favorable conditions for the practice of Dharma, 6. Dedication that worldly regions become successful and virtuous.
segments.translation_html:
This has six sections:
1. Dedication to obtain body and wealth,
2. Dedication to possess beauty and dignity,
3. Dedication to find magnificent virtue,
4. Dedication to obtain immaculate pure realms,
5. Dedication to accomplish favorable conditions for the practice of Dharma,
6. Dedication that worldly regions become successful and virtuous.

segments.translation_html:
May all be free from lack of any leisure,
Possessed of faith, wisdom, and compassion,
Successful in food and conduct,
And always remember their lives.

segments.translation_text: May all those who are not free from the eight unfavorable conditions be completely freed from them and obtain a precious human body with all of the correct endowments. There, may they possess the three types of faith: believing, clear, and desiring faith; the wisdom to understand both relative and ultimate phenomena; and heartfelt compassion toward each and every sentient being. May they be possessed of genuine moral conduct, a fine physical form and obtain good nutritious food. In each and every life, may they remember all of their previous lives and possess clairvoyance.

segments.translation_html:
May all find inexhaustible wealth,
Like the treasury of space.
Without quarreling and harm,
May they enjoy it freely.

segments.translation_text: May each and every sentient being attain the meditative absorption of the treasury of space. May they obtain inexhaustible material without any difficulties according to Dharma, as if everything appeared from space. May they never quarrel, fight, argue, harm, or injure each other for the purpose of material gain. May they joyfully and freely experience whatever they wish according to their capacity and power.

Through this merit of mine, May every sentient being without exception Abandon all sin And perform virtue always.[p.452][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]
Gyaltsen, Lama Kalsang, and Ani Kunga Chodron, trans. ''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. Walden, NY: Tsechen Kunchab Ling, 2019. First edition published by The Yeshe Dorje Foundation in 2006.

[[Texts/Bodhicaryāvatāra/Verses/10.32|Verse 10.32]]  ·  [[Translation Memory:001-Tsadra-BCA-Root-Padmakara/910|Verse tm]]
segments.translation_html:
Never parting from enlightenment thought,
Striving in the conduct of the Bodhisattvas,
Completely held by the Buddhas,
May all demonic actions be abandoned.

segments.wylie: khyad par du bsam pa byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa dang mi 'bral zhing sbyor ba pha rol tu phyin pas gzhan gyi don sgrub pa'i byang chub kyi spyod pa la gzhol ba dang grogs sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis yongs su bzung zhing mi mthun phyogs 'du 'dzi dang rnam g.yeng la sogs pa bdud kyi las thams cad kyang spangs par shog cig
segments.translation_text: Especially, may they never part from generating excellent enlightenment thought as a motivation, and through the practice of the six perfections perform the benefit of other beings as an application. Thus may they constantly engage in the conduct of Bodhisattvas. May they always be held by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as special friends. May they also completely abandon all demonic actions such as adverse conditions for the practice of Dharma, distractions, and mundane activities.

segments.translation_html:

Achieve limitless life,
And live in happiness always.
May even the word "death” never come to them.

[[Texts/Bodhicaryāvatāra/Verses/10.34|Verse 10.34]]  ·  [[Translation Memory:001-Tsadra-BCA-Root-Padmakara/912|Verse tm]]
segments.translation_html:
May all directions be filled with
Pleasant groves of wish-fulfilling trees,
Completely filled with the Buddha and his Noble Sons 
Proclaiming the melodious sound of Dharma teachings.

segments.translation_html:

May there dwell many Bodhisattvas
Adorned by their own good qualities,
Filling the entire earth.

Harvests be successful,
Rulers act according to Dharma,
And worldly beings also flourish.

segments.translation_text: Likewise, may all renunciates who wish to attain liberation renounce their home, wander homelessly, and be able to preserve morality without decline in their moral commitments, which helps to cool the heat of the defilements. In case of lapses of morality or breaking of rules, may they strongly regret it and repair their vows immediately. May they completely exhaust all sins and unwholesome deeds and be completely purified. Temporarily may they always attain higher rebirth, become renunciates, and observe moral conduct without decline.

In case of lapses of morality or breaking of rules, may they strongly regret it and repair their vows immediately. May they completely exhaust all sins and unwholesome deeds and be completely purified. Temporarily may they always attain higher rebirth, become renunciates, and observe moral conduct without decline.

segments.translation_text: Temporarily, may scholars never experience the suffering of the lower realms. segments.translation_html:
May I, too, through the grace of Manjushri,
Until attaining the stage of extreme joy,
Always remember my lives,
And well obtain ordination.

segments.translation_text: May I, the author, rely upon the watchful protection and kindness of Manjushri, most exalted among my deities, until I reach the state of extreme joy, the stage of a first bumi Bodhisattva. May I be able to constantly recall my previous life and all lives prior to that, and develop strong trust in the cause and result of actions. In every life, may I be able to take the immaculate vows of a fully ordained monk, which is the foundation of all positive qualities.

segments.translation_html:
When I wish to gaze
Or even slightly wish to ask,
May I behold without hindrance
The Protector Manjushri himself.

segments.translation_text: Whenever I wish to gaze upon the holy body or wish to ask even the slightest question about the meaning of Dharma, at that moment, may I be able to perceive Manjushri himself, protector of all worldly beings, directly without any obscuration or hindrance. In every situation, may I be protected and closely guarded by him.

[[Texts/Bodhicaryāvatāra/Verses/10.54|Verse 10.54]]  ·  [[Translation Memory:001-Tsadra-BCA-Root-Padmakara/932|Verse tm]]
segments.translation_html:
To accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings,
Equal to the boundary of space in the ten directions, 
Whatever conduct Manjushri performed,
May my own conduct become just like that.

segments.wylie: phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams rab 'byams nam mkha'i mthas gtugs par khyab pa'i sems can ma lus pa kun gyi gnas skabs dang mthar thug gi don thams cad bde blag tu bsgrub pa'i phyir ji ltar 'phags pa 'jam dpal la sogs pa byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa rlabs po che gzhan la phan pa 'ba' zhig mdzad pa bzhin du bdag gi spyod pa'ang de 'dra ba kho nar gzhan la phan pa 'ba' zhig 'grub par shog cig
segments.translation_text: May I swiftly accomplish all temporary and ultimate purposes for each and every sentient being without any exception in all the infinite realms of the ten directions throughout boundless space. Just as Manjushri and other great Bodhisattvas entered the great wave of the Bodhisattva’s conduct in order to perform only the benefit and welfare of other beings, so too, may I accomplish only the benefit and welfare of other beings.

segments.translation_html:
However long space abides,
However long beings abide,
That long may I abide,
To dispel the suffering of beings.

segments.translation_text: For as long as space endures, as long as all sentient beings without exception abide, so too, may I abide without entering into nirvana to perform the benefit of other beings. As a result of my activities, may I be able to dispel every form of suffering for the infinite sentient beings dwelling in the agonies of lower birth and samsara.

''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. segments.translation_html:
May the Doctrine,
The sole medicine for beings' suffering, and
The source of every happiness.
Endure long with honor and veneration.

segments.wylie: gro ba mtha' yas pa'i 'khor ba dang ngan song gi sdug bsngal gyi nad thams cad sel ba'i sman gyi mchog gcig pur gyur cing*/_mtho ris dang thar pa'i bde ba phun sum tshogs pa kun 'byung ba'i gnas dam par gyur pa sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa rin po che lung dang rtogs pa'i bdag nyid can 'chad nyan dang sgrub pa'i sgo nas bzung zhing rnyed pa dang bkur sti'i mchod pa rgya chen po dang bcas te dus yun ring po'i bar du 'jig rten 'dir gnas par gyur cig ces pa'o/_/
segments.translation_text: The precious doctrine of the Buddha, which is embodied in scripture and realization, is the only excellent medicine that can dispel every suffering of the lower realms as well as every suffering of the infinite samsaric sentient beings, and is the only excellent medicine that is the source of the arising of every form of happiness and success of higher rebirth. May this precious doctrine be upheld through the practice of study and explication, and remain in the world with elaborate offerings and veneration for a very long time.

segments.translation_html:
I prostrate to Manjushri,
By whose kindness thoughts of virtue arise,
I prostrate to the spiritual master
By whose kindness I succeed.

segments.translation_text: By the blessings and kindness of the most of exalted of deities, who possesses great compassion, may I abandon attachment to all essenceless worldly activities and singlepointedly exert myself only in the virtuous activities of study, contemplation, and meditation. Having been blessed by special intellectual knowledge through the kindness of the Bhagwan protector, Manjushri, I prostrate to him through great devotion of body, voice, and mind. As it is said:

segments.translation_text: The root text, Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas was initially composed in the Sanskrit language in India, the land of holy beings. From there, earlier noble beings brought it to Tibet during the period of the flourishing of the Buddha’s doctrine. Initially, the great Indian master Sarva Gyana Deva (All-Knowing God) and the great translator and editor Bhante Paltsik, translated it into the Tibetan language from a Kashmiri text, edited it, and performed vast benefit to the fortunate through teaching and listening to the text.

segments.translation_html:
Although many scholars taught this immaculate text,
In order to swiftly realize the many exalted meanings in clear words,
This explication was requested by many possessing intellectual analysis and sincerity,
And was written by Lodu Gyaltsen in order to develop immaculate motivation and application.

segments.translation_text: May naturally pure sentient beings equal to the bounds of space Develop exalted enlightenment thought in their minds as a motivation. Excellently engage in the six perfections as an application, And swiftly reach great enlightenment as a result.
segments.translation_html:
May naturally pure sentient beings equal to the bounds of space
Develop exalted enlightenment thought in their minds as a motivation.
Excellently engage in the six perfections as an application,
And swiftly reach great enlightenment as a result.

segments.translation_text: Until then, may the sun and moon-like doctrine of the Buddha clearly shine upon the islands of disciples, Dispel the foggy vision of dark ignorance, generate the light ofprimordial wisdom, and Cause all beings to completely abandon evil intentions and applications of harming each other. And day and night, with kindness and compassion practice the holy Dharma.
segments.translation_html:
Until then, may the sun and moon-like doctrine of the Buddha clearly shine upon the islands of disciples,
Dispel the foggy vision of dark ignorance, generate the light ofprimordial wisdom, and
Cause all beings to completely abandon evil intentions and applications of harming each other.
And day and night, with kindness and compassion practice the holy Dharma.

segments.translation_text: This text, A Commentary on Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas, Known as an Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text was composed by the Tibetan Pandita Jamyang Lodu, who has achieved some clarity of intellect concerning the five sciences, based on the kindness of the noble, holy lamas. This was written at Champa Ling Monastery. May it be of great benefit for a multitude of sentient beings and the precious Buddha’s doctrine.
segments.translation_html: This text, A Commentary on Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas, Known as an Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text was composed by the Tibetan Pandita Jamyang Lodu,68Pandita Jamyang Lodu is also known as Sazang Mati Panchen. who has achieved some clarity of intellect concerning the five sciences, based on the kindness of the noble, holy lamas. This was written at Champa Ling Monastery. May it be of great benefit for a multitude of sentient beings and the precious Buddha’s doctrine.
